clinical_trigger: established ASCVD or high CVD risk
summary_text: For type 2 diabetes with established or high ASCVD risk, include a GLP-1 RA and/or SGLT2 inhibitor with cardiovascular benefit irrespective of A1c.
retrieval_keywords: ASCVD CVD GLP-1 SGLT2 cardiovascular benefit

clinical_trigger: heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction
summary_text: For type 2 diabetes with heart failure, recommend an SGLT2 inhibitor for glycemic management and prevention of HF hospitalization irrespective of A1c.
For type 2 diabetes with CKD, use an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA with demonstrated benefit for glycemic management, CKD progression, and cardiovascular event reduction.
For type 2 diabetes with advanced CKD, GLP-1 RA is preferred for glycemic management because of lower hypoglycemia risk and cardiovascular benefit.

clinical_trigger: concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA
summary_text: Concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor use with GLP-1 RA or dual GIP/GLP-1 RA is not recommended because it adds no glucose-lowering benefit.
Insulin initiation should be considered when symptoms are present or A1c/glucose levels are very high.
Without severe hyperglycemia or crisis, GLP-1-based therapy is preferred to insulin for initial or add-on glucose-lowering therapy.
If insulin is used, GLP-1 RA combination is recommended for glycemic effectiveness and benefits on weight and hypoglycemia risk; insulin dosing should be reassessed.
Metformin is generally safe at eGFR >=30; risk rises when eGFR is below 30, and eGFR 30-45 warrants caution.
